title: Tamsin and the Debt
premise: Freya 'Tamsin' Thornbury, a disgraced intelligence analyst working deniable cases from a network of safe houses, discovers her current bolthole listed online with interior photos that include her own face in a mirror. The listing is a message from the Meridian Group, the syndicate she helped expose years ago and the reason she's been erased. They want the ledger she copied on her last official case — the one proving a sitting minister sold state secrets. As Meridian hunts her through the found family of misfits she's assembled, Tamsin must decide whether to trade the ledger for their lives or use it to burn Meridian down. In the end she leaks the ledger publicly, sacrificing her own anonymity forever, but the family survives scattered and alive — and Meridian's minister falls.
about_author: Gideon Crane is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade adjacent to the world of contractors, cutouts, and quiet firings. They write thrillers about people the system discards and the debts it never forgives.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Scrolling property sites out of boredom, she finds her safe house listed with photos of the interior — including her reflection. The emotional beat is cold dread: invisibility was an illusion. She burns the hard drives and wakes the others.

chapters.title: House of Strangers
chapters.summary: Dez, the forger, POV. Introduces the found family: Dez, hacker Wren, ex-cop Mabry, and runner Ivo. Dez resents the disruption but reveals the family's fragile loyalty rules. Emotional beat: belonging built on shared damage.

chapters.title: Terms of Sale
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. A burner message arrives: an open-house invitation with a time and address. Meridian wants the ledger. Flashback seeds the night she copied it and the minister's name. Beat: guilt resurfacing — she brought this to their door.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Mabry, POV. Mabry scouts the open house and recognizes a Meridian fixer, Calloway, from an old case. A near-miss in the hallway. Beat: the enemy is professional, patient, and already inside their old lives.

chapters.title: What Wren Found
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren traces the listing to a shell agency and finds the photos were taken weeks ago — Meridian has watched them far longer than anyone knew. Beat: paranoia curdling into the realization that someone close may have slipped.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. She opens the encrypted drive and walks the reader through what's on it: payments, dates, and the minister's signature. Beat: temptation — the ledger is her only leverage, and her only death sentence.

chapters.title: Ivo Runs
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Sent to a dead-drop contact, Ivo is followed and barely escapes, wounded. He hides the fact. Beat: pride and fear — the family's youngest lying to protect them, and failing.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, No Friends
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. She reaches out to a former handler, Voss, who once burned her. Voss offers protection in exchange for the ledger. Beat: bitterness and the seduction of being wanted back.

chapters.title: Safe Houses Fall
chapters.summary: Dez, POV. A second bolt-hole is raided; Dez's documents and plates are seized. The family scatters to a canal boat. Beat: grief for the infrastructure of their hidden life, and resolve forming.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Calloway, POV. The antagonist chapter: his methodical, almost tender persuasion, and his own orders from above — the minister wants the ledger and the witnesses gone. Beat: chilling competence; evil as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: The Mole Question
chapters.summary: Mabry, POV. Mabry interrogates the family's contacts and finds the leak trail leads inward — to Ivo's wounded escape and the phone he kept. Beat: betrayal that isn't quite betrayal; loyalty under pressure.

chapters.title: Confession on the Water
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo admits everything to Tamsin on the canal at night. She doesn't forgive; she weaponizes his mistake — a controlled channel to feed Meridian false locations. Beat: shame transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Voss's Net
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Voss's protection turns out to be a trap to seize the ledger for the agency's own leverage. Tamsin escapes, burning the last bridge to her old life. Beat: the system itself is a predator.

chapters.title: The Minister's Wife
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren uncovers that the minister's wife has been quietly moving money — a second ledger, a private one. A fragile contact is made. Beat: hope; an unexpected door in the wall.

chapters.title: Exchange Terms
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Meridian proposes a trade: the ledger for the family's clean exits. Tamsin agrees to a meet, secretly planning to swap in a doctored copy. Beat: cold resolve; she's become the thing she fled.

chapters.title: Forged and True
chapters.summary: Dez, POV. Dez builds the forgery while wrestling with what a fake ledger does to real people — including the wife now helping them. Beat: the ethics of survival; craft as conscience.

chapters.title: The Meet at Blackwall
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Mabry, POV. The exchange at a derelict pier goes wrong — Calloway expected the forgery and takes Ivo instead. Beat: the plan's collapse; the price of cleverness.

chapters.title: Hostage
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo endures interrogation, giving up nothing real but buying time with a planted lie about the ledger's location. Beat: courage from the family's weakest link.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Climax: instead of trading, Tamsin releases the full ledger — real and wife's private copy — to the press and public registries simultaneously. The rescue of Ivo becomes chaos as Meridian's machinery turns on itself. Beat: the secret spent, no going back.

chapters.title: Calloway's Last Errand
chapters.summary: Calloway, POV. His masters disown him; ordered to disappear, he instead tries to salvage his pension by selling Tamsin's location — to Voss. Mabry intercepts. Beat: the machine devouring its own.

chapters.title: The Minister Falls
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Aftermath in motion: resignations, arrests, the wife's testimony. Meridian's remnants scatter. The family regroups, bruised, on the canal boat. Beat: victory that feels like ash; the debt partially paid.

chapters.title: Tamsin, In the Open
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Her face is now public; anonymity is gone forever. But the family chooses to stay together under new names, in daylight, running a legitimate investigations shop. Beat: found family as the true safe house; survival's price was her invisibility, and it was worth it.
